_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::contact#11 — being listed by `4C --parameters` is necessary, not sufficient. Four runs of one two-block mortar deck (-0.3 over ten steps) plus a read of the binary's own schema, run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. Observed: the STRATEGY Penalty control exits 0 with 'processor 0 finished normally'; STRATEGY: "Uzawa" exits 1 with 'This contact strategy is not yet considered!' from contact/4C_contact_strategy_factory.cpp line 1628; and 'SEMI_SMOOTH_NEWTON: false' — a perfectly valid boolean — exits 1 with 'Currently we support only the semi-smooth Newton case!' from contact/4C_contact_noxinterface.cpp line 264. The 'it IS listed' half is evidence rather than assertion: the fixture runs `4C --parameters` itself and reports UZAWA_IS_IN_THE_STRATEGY_ENUM=yes and SEMI_SMOOTH_NEWTON_IS_A_DOCUMENTED_KEY=yes. A fourth arm shows the schema really does filter, so 'it parsed' is not vacuous either: a STRATEGY value that is NOT in the enum (STEAMROLLER_IS_IN_THE_STRATEGY_ENUM=no) is refused earlier and with a different message, 'Could not match this input', and never reaches the strategy factory at all (UNKNOWN_STRATEGY_REACHED_THE_FACTORY=0).
expect_in_output: This contact strategy is not yet considered!
Currently we support only the semi-smooth Newton case!

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: pick a strategy the code actually implements. 'This contact strategy is not yet considered!' disappears and EXIT_UZAWA becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the semi-smooth arm: leave the key at its default. The noxinterface abort disappears and EXIT_NO_SEMISMOOTH becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
